props.gloss_en: a chicken -- twenty-one days
and its counterpart among trees -- the almond
a dog -- fifty days
its counterpart among trees -- the fig
a cat -- fifty-two days
its counterpart among trees -- the mulberry
a pig -- sixty days
its counterpart among trees -- the apple

their counterpart among plants -- grain
small kosher livestock -- five months

large non-kosher livestock -- twelve months

its counterpart among trees -- the olive

their counterpart among trees -- white figs (bnot shuach)
a viper -- seventy years
its counterpart among trees -- the carob
this carob: from its planting to the ripening of its fruit, seventy years; and its days of 'gestation' three years
a snake -- seven years
and for that wicked one we have found no fellow [among trees]
and some say: mukhsasim [are its counterpart]
the snake's seven years derive from 'cursed are you beyond all the behema and beyond all the beasts of the field' (Bereshit 3:14)
since 'beyond chaya' would follow a fortiori from 'beyond behema', the clause comes to teach: the snake was cursed beyond behema in the same proportion as behema was cursed beyond chaya
behema was cursed beyond chaya one to seven
and which is it? the donkey beyond the cat [twelve months against fifty-two days]
so the snake was cursed beyond behema one to seven, which makes seven years
say: as chaya was cursed beyond behema one to three (lion beyond donkey), so the snake beyond chaya one to three -- nine years
and say: as behema was cursed beyond chaya one to three (goat beyond cat), so the snake beyond behema one to three -- fifteen months
but the elders of Athens mated them and they bore after three [years]
those were already pregnant four [years] beforehand
they too mate as a human does [not only for conception]
we are wiser than they
I am the sage of the Jews, I wish to learn wisdom from you; if you win, do with me as you wish, and if I win, eat with me on the ship
to 'why would a man refused a wife go to a greater family?': [the peg enters the upper hole, not the lower wall] -- he too may chance on his destined match
to 'why does a lender whose loan was lost lend again?': one who cuts a bundle he cannot lift cuts more and adds to it, until someone chances by to lift it for him
to 'tell us nonsense': a mule gave birth, with a note owing it 100,000 zuz from its father's house -- 'can a mule give birth?' -- that is the nonsense
to 'with what does one salt spoiled salt?': with a mule's afterbirth -- 'does a mule have an afterbirth?' -- 'and does salt spoil?'
to 'build us a house in the air': [hovering by a Name] bring me up bricks and mortar
to 'where is the middle of the world?': here -- and if you doubt it, bring ropes and measure
to 'bring our field-pit into town': braid me ropes of bran; to 'sew our broken mill': pull me threads from it
to 'with what does one reap a field of knives?': with a donkey's horn -- 'is there a donkey's horn?' -- 'is there a field of knives?'
to the two eggs (which from the black hen, which from the white?): two cheeses -- which from the black goat, which from the white?
to 'a chick dead in the egg -- whence does its spirit leave?': whence it entered, it left
to 'show us a vessel not worth its damage': [the spread mat that will not pass the gate] bring axes and break it down -- this is a vessel not worth its damage
the emperor, seeing them wretched: these are not they
the emperor, after they grew insolent before him: do with them whatever you wish
RYbC to the elders: fill it [the vessel holding the water of the House of the Swallowed] and go your way -- they filled until their shoulders gave and were swallowed
